commitResults.messageTitle: Find students by part of their name with n/
commitResults.messageBody:
find matches only whole words in a student's name, so a tutor who
remembers only part of a name, such as "avi" for David, gets no
results. This is the case UC4 covers: finding a student quickly while
a guardian is on the phone.

Change find to take a single n/ value and match it anywhere in the
name, ignoring case. The value is matched as one piece of text, so
"loe tan" finds Chloe Tan but "tan loe" does not. Runs of spaces in
the value are squeezed to one.

Reject a blank value, because every name contains the empty string
and the search would match every student. Reject a repeated n/ and
any text before it, so a mistyped command shows an error instead of
silently searching for something else.

Lowercase with Locale.ROOT, so the result does not depend on the
computer's language setting. In a Turkish locale, "IDA" lowercases
to "ıda", and find would miss a student named Ida.

The name predicate keeps its list of keywords, although the parser
now always passes one. Changing its constructor would touch test
files that open PRs are also editing, so that cleanup is left for
after they merge.
